title: Strategic sprint orchestration compact
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact, actionable playbook to align the next 12 weeks across product, engineering, SRE, and GTM ahead of the spring company-wide cadence (town + exec updates + OKR refresh). The doc synthesizes candidate OKRs, a proposed exec update narrative, the all-hands run-of-show micro-slate, and a short decision timetable.

Principles driving the plan:
- Keep the company north star simple: predictable inference economics + developer velocity.
- Prioritize reliability and cost efficiency where customers see immediate impact.
- Limit the number of cross-org OKRs to 3 to ensure focus.
- Use short, measurable experiments for any risky bets (A/B, canary, rollback plan).

Candidate company-level OKRs (shortlist for exec alignment):
1) OKR: Deliver 30% system cost-per-token reduction for hosted API workloads (Q2 target)
   - Key results:
     - KR1: Reduce average token compute cost by 20% from baseline via batching + model mix recommendations (owner: Platform Economics / Lina Alvarez)
     - KR2: Increase KV/prefix cache hit rate from 12% -> 40% on top-50 routes (owner: Serving Runtime / Priya Singh)
     - KR3: Validate two quantized model variants with parity for top 3 customer prompt sets (owner: Applied ML / Ethan Kim)

2) OKR: Establish Dedicated capacity baseline and SLA for two reference customers (Q2 pilot -> Q3 GA)
   - Key results:
     - KR1: Document and ship Dedicated onboarding playbook + automated infra templates (owner: Solutions Eng)
     - KR2: Achieve 95th pct latency SLAs across piloted workloads (owner: Dedicated infra lead)
     - KR3: Close at least one pay-committed pilot contract (owner: Sales)

3) OKR: Reduce production incidents affecting customer-facing latency by 40%
   - Key results:
     - KR1: Postmortem backlog <= 5 unresolved incidents older than 30 days (owner: SRE)
     - KR2: Implement region-aware fallback routing for two top regions (owner: Platform Engineering)
     - KR3: Add token-level tracing on 5 highest-traffic routes (owner: Observability)

Notes on prioritization:
- If cost-per-token reductions trend slower than expected, shift resource from non-critical roadmap items (feature parity with legacy endpoints) to runtime optimizations.
- Dedicated pilot is a high-sales-leverage item; treat onboarding docs and infra templates as launch-critical.

Exec update narrative (5 minute spoken + 1 slide):
- One-liner: We are optimizing for predictable inference economics and reliability so customers can run at scale without surprise bills or latency spikes.
- What we shipped/validated since last update (30s): KV caching prototype with early 25% token reduction on small testbed; Dedicated pilot signed LOI with two customers; trace sampling landed.
- Current top risks (30s): Cache correctness regressions on edge prompts; Dedicated SLA tuning might require hardware rebalancing; model quantization quality drift on long sequences.
- Decisions we need from execs this week (30s): Approve shifting one infra pod from feature roadmap to caching performance work (cost tradeoff), greenlight a small contract incentive for pilot customers.
- Ask of the company / all-hands call (30s): Be prepared for a 2-week engineering focus window starting Mar 3 to get the cache rollout into staging.

All-hands mini run-of-show (20–25 minutes total):
- 0:00–02:00 — CEO (Noah): company context and the one-liner above
- 02:00–07:00 — Product/Platform highlight (Asha + Ethan): demo of cache hit-rate UI + quick before/after metric
- 07:00–12:00 — Customer story (Solutions Eng): pilot customer notes and what Dedicated means operationally
- 12:00–15:00 — Reliability primer (Priya): how fallback/rollout will work and how SRE will reduce incident surface
- 15:00–20:00 — People and ops: hiring snapshot, hiring freezes (if any), and where teams should pause work
- 20:00–25:00 — Q&A + live decision poll (Slack emoji vote integrated)

Communications timeline (compressed):
- Feb 18 — Exec alignment + sign off on candidate OKRs (this week)
- Feb 19–28 — Team-level OKR writeups and measurement plans (owner: team leads)
- Mar 3 — Company focus window start (2 weeks) + all-hands to announce and demo
- Mar 17 — Midpoint pulse and short exec check-in (15m)

Decision log (what we need now):
- Approve company OKR shortlist (Asha to capture final wording).
- Exec sign-off on re-prioritizing 1 infra pod for caching work (Ethan to confirm resource shift).
- Budget approval for pilot incentives up to $X (Finance + Sales).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How to measure customer-visible cost reductions precisely given current billing granularity? (Finance + Platform Economics to propose measurement plan by Feb 25)
- What is the rollback threshold for cache behavioral regressions? (SRE + Applied ML)
- Should we add a 4th OKR focused purely on Developer DX (SDKs/Docs)? Pros: increases adoption; Cons: dilutes focus. Vote suggested during exec meeting.

Risks and contingency plans:
- Risk: Cache introduces correctness regressions in edge prompts -> Contingency: Preset canary to 5% of traffic, immediate auto-roll back and flagging to product owners.
- Risk: Quantized model quality drop on long context -> Contingency: Keep non-quantized variant in region fallback pools until A/B shows parity.
- Risk: Dedicated pilot delays due to infra mismatch -> Contingency: Offer short-term hosted credits and manual SLA guardrails while infra templates mature.

Metrics dashboard (minimum set to publish for the all-hands):
- Company cost-per-token (moving avg)
- Cache hit rate (top-50 routes)
- 95th pct latency (top-10 routes)
- Incidents by severity (30-day window)
- Dedicated pilot onboarding progress (checklist completion %)

Immediate action items (owners + due dates):
- Asha: finalize OKR wording and publish to confluence (due Feb 19).
- Ethan: confirm infra pod reallocation and list impacted features (due Feb 20).
- Priya: implement canary gating for cache rollout and push SRE runbook (due Feb 25).
- Lina: finalize cost measurement plan and baseline (due Feb 25).
- Sales: prepare pilot incentive outline for Finance review (due Feb 22).

Appendix: short experiment templates (placeholders)
- Experiment: Cache prefix tuning on route X
  - Hypothesis: tuning TTL + grouping reduces downstream compute by 15% without affecting correctness
  - Metric: per-route token compute change, false positive rate on prompt checks
  - Rollback: revert config via rollout matrix if correctness regression > 0.5%

Quick notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact. Expect more detailed team-level OKR drafts to appear in the next 48 hours in the linked Confluence page.
- If you are a team lead and cannot meet dates above, please add a blocker comment in the Confluence page and tag me (@Asha).

End of doc.
